name: Pale black hue
lede: Pale black hue is a near-black plum, filed under a traditional Japanese name, Shikon, meaning blue-violet.

sections.title: Blue-violet, very dark
sections.body:
Our library lists this swatch as *Shikon* (紫紺), literally "blue-violet," one of the traditional colors of Japan recorded on Wikipedia's list of that name [1]. The English label "Pale black hue" is this app's own rendering and not a separate historical term; who first used the Japanese name, and when, is not documented in the sources checked here [1]. Our library also crosses this same swatch to three ISCC-NBS 1955 block names, Admiral, Logwood and Sailor, and to Maerz and Paul's Neutral Tin, first recorded about 1804 [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[vivid-black]], only 2.9 units off, essentially the same color on screen [2]; [[continental-blue]] sits 3.4 units away. It shares its exact hex with the related swatch [[pale-black-shade]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color within range of this swatch in 618 of 23,781 paintings, 2.6 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 518 [3]. It most often plays a shadow, in 46 percent of those 518 paintings by lightness rank, so varnish cannot fake the result [3]. George Dawe painted it most often among individual painters, in 7 of his 50 works here, though no painter stands out against the museum baseline [3]. The earliest match dates to the year 1201, long before any record of the Japanese name, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].
